title: Feature Owner Stability Handbook and Rapid Escalation Templates
content:
Purpose and scope:
This handbook is targeted at feature owners, PMs, and engineers who are shipping services that surface to Redwood customers. It provides a compact, actionable SLO adoption playbook, onboarding checklists, rapid-escalation templates for oncall rotation changes, and lightweight verification experiments to validate SLOs before rollout.

Background & problem statement:
Feature teams frequently ship behavioural changes without explicit SLOs or clear ownership for availability/latency. That leads to firefighting, surprise customer incidents, and inconsistent oncall expectations. This doc is a cross-functional contract: product + eng + SRE agree on minimal stability commitments and a rapid escalation path.

Objectives (SMART):
- Define and onboard 12 active feature teams to a minimum set of SLOs and runbooks within 90 days.
- Reduce first-response MTTR for customer-impacting incidents by 30% for participating teams within 60 days.
- Establish automated signal collection and a monthly dashboard per-team within 45 days.

Minimum SLO template (for feature owners):
- Availability SLO: 99.9% successful request rate measured at the API gateway over a 30-day window.
- Latency SLO: 95th percentile tail latency <= 300ms for standard gen endpoints, collected as end-to-end (ingress->egress).
- Error budget policy: 25% of error budget can be consumed for non-customer-facing experiments; any further consumption requires SRE review and canary rollback.

Roles & responsibilities:
- Feature Owner (FO): owns SLO targets, customer impact matrix, and runbook updates.
- Service Reliability Engineer (SRE): helps define meaningful signals, configures alerting thresholds, and triages early incidents.
- Product Manager (PM): approves business-critical availability targets and communicates changes to stakeholders.
- Oncall engineer: executes rapid-escalation templates and coordinates immediate mitigations.

30/60/90 day activation plan:
- Day 0-14: Rapid assessment. FO fills the lightweight SLO intake form (link in linked_artifacts). SRE runs a short signal-mapping session to surface current telemetry gaps.
- Day 15-45: Instrumentation and baseline. Add telemetry hooks (success/error counters, latency histograms, cache hit ratio). Configure dashboards and error budget panels. Run two synthetic traffic checks.
- Day 46-75: Runbook draft and table-top. Create a 1-page runbook for the critical user flows, map escalation contacts, simulate a 30-minute table-top incident.
- Day 76-90: Canary & adoption. Enable a guarded rollout where 5–10% of traffic uses the new flow or feature behind a canary flag. Observe error budget burn and adjust. Declare SLO adoption and schedule monthly cadence.

Rapid escalation templates (use in pager or Slack):
- Pager title: "P0: [service-name] - customer-impacting errors"
  Body: "Impact: [one-line], Start: [timestamp], Symptoms: [one-line], Immediate mitigation: [step], Runbook ref: [link], Pager contact: @oncall-team"

- Slack template (incident channel pinned):
  1) Subject: P0 - [service] - customer impact
  2) One-line summary + visible owner
  3) Current hypothesis + action in-flight
  4) Next check-in cadence (5m)

Incident triage checklist (first 15 minutes):
1) Confirm impact and scope (internal vs customer-visible).
2) Identify fallback paths and enable them (traffic split, degrade model size).
3) Snapshot logs and start short-term traces for 5 samples.
4) Notify PM and CS if customer impact > 1% of daily active requests.
5) Create incident channel and apply the slack template.

Runbook one-pager structure (must be <= 1 page):
- Service summary and owner contacts
- How to verify service health (key metrics and queries)
- Quick mitigations (3 steps max with command snippets)
- Escalation path (names + phone/pager)
- Post-incident actions and SLO check

Measurement and telemetry checklist:
- End-to-end request success rate (gateway-level)
- Latency p50/p95/p99 with request-type tags
- Error class breakdown (4xx/5xx/model-timeouts)
- Dependency health (datastore, auth, external APIs)
- Synthetic canary checks every 5 minutes

Operational cadence & decision rituals:
- Weekly SLO sync (30 minutes) between FO and SRE for the first 8 weeks. Agenda: signal review, error budget consumption, mitigation decisions.
- Monthly reliability review with PM, SRE, and CS (45 minutes). Outcome: adoption decision, rollout approvals.
- Quarterly tabletop incident drill for participating teams.

Onboarding kit (deliverables per team):
1) Completed SLO intake form
2) One-page runbook committed to repo and Confluence
3) Dashboards and alerting in place with thresholds and action steps
4) Canary plan and rollback criteria documented
5) Oncall rotation entry with contacts updated

Training modules (self-serve + live):
- Self-serve: 20 minute video walkthrough of the one-page runbook and instrumentation checklist.
- Live: 90 minute hands-on workshop run by SREs to simulate a canary and run a table-top incident.

Communication templates:
- Pre-rollout notice for stakeholders (email/Slack): short summary of SLO, rollout timing, expected risk and rollback plan.
- Post-incident customer-facing message (CS to adapt): brief explanation, user impact, mitigation and follow-up actions.

Risk register (top risks and mitigations):
- Risk: Missing observability in critical path. Mitigation: Fail fast policy for instrumentation with a 2-week remediation SLA.
- Risk: Overly aggressive SLO targets cause frequent toil. Mitigation: Start conservative; iterate after baseline measurement.
- Risk: Confusion over ownership across infra boundaries. Mitigation: Escalation matrix with explicit primary and secondary owners.

Open questions and decision log (short):
- Q: Should we standardize on a single latency SLO for all gen endpoints? A: Deferred — allow team-specific tail targets but standardize measurement method.
- Q: Can we automate rollback when error budget burn > X%? A: Pilot scheduled; action requires manual SRE confirmation for first 2 quarters.

Appendix: quick commands and dashboard queries (examples)
- Gateway success rate: sum(success_count) / sum(total_count) by service over 30d
- Tail latency: histogram_quantile(0.95, rate(request_duration_bucket[5m]))

Next steps / owner actions this week:
- FO: complete SLO intake and schedule the signal-mapping session with SRE (due in 7 days).
- SRE: provision dashboard template and a synthetic canary for the service (due in 10 days).
- PM: confirm customer-impact threshold that triggers CS notification (due in 7 days).

Contact and feedback:
For questions or to request help with onboarding, ping #sre-ops or email priya.nair@redwood.com. This document is intended as a living handbook; please add concrete playbook edits to the Confluence page referenced in linked_artifacts.
